name: Mass Email Notifications for Gravity Forms – Lite
author: BrightLeaf Digital

sections.description:
Mass Email Notifications for Gravity Forms is a powerful plugin designed to extend the capabilities of your Gravity Forms by allowing you to send mass email notifications to users who have previously filled out any form on your site.

Whether you’re running a campaign, sending updates, or simply notifying a specific group of respondents, this plugin makes it easy to reach your audience with just one form submission.

By leveraging Gravity Forms’ built-in email fields and intuitive interface, you can send personalized notifications to multiple recipients with ease.

For advanced users, the premium version offers robust filtering options, allowing you to target specific entries based on conditional logic.

Key Features:

  • Bulk Send Notifications: This feature allows you to send mass email notifications to all entries from a selected Gravity Form. Whether you’re targeting a large group or just a few recipients, you can do it all with a single form submission. This is perfect for sending newsletters, updates, or reminders without the need to manually enter each email address.
  • Conditional Logic Filtering: With the premium version, you can refine your email targets using conditional logic. This means you can filter entries based on any field within the target form, such as specific responses, dates, or custom criteria. This feature ensures that your emails are sent only to the most relevant recipients, enhancing the effectiveness of your communication.
  • Double Opt-In Verification (Premium): Ensure a high-quality email list by requiring recipients to confirm their subscription. You can restrict mass emails to only those who have explicitly opted in via a confirmation link.
  • Gravity Flow Integration (Premium): Seamlessly integrate with Gravity Flow to (re)start workflows on double opt-in, delay workflow steps until confirmation, and manage “Mass Email Notification Batch” workflow steps directly from the plugin dashboard.
  • Custom Unsubscribe/Preferences Landing Page (Premium): Instead of a generic unsubscribe link, use a custom Gravity Form as a landing page to allow users to manage their preferences, pause their subscription, or unsubscribe from specific topics. Choose whether an unsubscribe stops only the feed it came from or every mass email from the site.
  • Unsubscribe Compliance: Optional unsubscribe link with a confirmation step that stops link scanners from unsubscribing people, and an optional mailing address added to every mass email.
  • Utilize Built-In Email Fields: The plugin fully integrates with Gravity Forms’ native email fields, ensuring seamless functionality. You don’t need to worry about compatibility issues or complex configurations—just select the email field from your form and start sending notifications immediately.
  • User-Friendly Interface: The plugin integrates directly within the Gravity Forms feed configuration area, providing a seamless experience. The intuitive interface makes it easy for users of all technical levels to set up and manage their mass email notifications. You can configure everything in just a few clicks, without needing to leave the familiar Gravity Forms environment.
  • Batch Management: View and manage your email batches directly from the settings page, allowing you to track the progress and status of your mass email campaigns.
  • CSV Import (Premium): Premium users can upload CSV files to add additional recipients to their email batches, providing more flexibility in managing recipient lists.
  • Email Throttling: Built-in but configurable email throttling ensures your mass emails stay within your hosting provider’s sending limits, preventing potential delivery issues.
  • GravityOps Dashboard: Manage batches, deliverability limits, feeds, unsubscribe preferences, and suppressions from dedicated tabs under GravityOps → Mass Notifications. Search feeds across forms and activate or deactivate them without reloading the page.

Benefits:

  • Efficient Communication: With the ability to send mass emails from a single form submission, you save time and effort. Instead of manually sending emails to each respondent, you can automate the process and ensure that everyone who needs to receive the message gets it immediately. This efficiency is crucial for large campaigns, event notifications, or any scenario where timely communication is key.
  • Targeted Messaging: The conditional logic feature in the premium version allows you to send targeted messages to specific respondents based on their form entries. This ensures that your communications are relevant and personalized, increasing engagement and response rates. For example, you could send follow-up emails only to users who expressed interest in a particular product or service.
  • Seamless Integration: By leveraging Gravity Forms’ existing email fields, the plugin integrates smoothly into your existing workflows. There’s no need for additional plugins or complex setups—everything works out of the box, reducing potential technical issues and ensuring a hassle-free experience.
  • User-Friendly Setup: The intuitive interface makes it easy to set up and manage mass email notifications, even for users with limited technical expertise. This accessibility means that anyone on your team can handle email campaigns, reducing the dependency on specialized knowledge or external help.
  • Scalable Solution: Whether you’re managing a small list or a large database of form entries, this plugin scales to meet your needs. As your business grows and your communication needs become more complex, the plugin can handle the increased load without compromising performance or reliability.

For more details please visit our plugin documentation page.

Note: This plugin works best when your website is configured to send emails via SMTP.

Community Help

For plugin support, contact BrightLeaf support.

For how-to questions and examples of what others have built, visit the GravityOps Help community.

If you opened a support thread on WordPress.org, continue that conversation there. The community is an additional place for help and ideas.

External services

Emails are sent through your site’s own mail setup. Your recipient lists and entries are never sent to BrightLeaf Digital.

The plugin connects to outside services only in these cases:

  • GravityOps product catalog. When an administrator uses the WordPress admin (or shortly afterwards, through WP-Cron), the shared GravityOps library downloads the GravityOps product catalog (names, versions, icons, links and announcements) from brightleafdigital.io, at most about twice a day. The request sends no personal data or site content; like any web request, it reveals your server’s IP address.
  • Newsletter signup. Only if you choose to subscribe to GravityOps Weekly, the email address you enter is sent to brightleafdigital.io.
  • Feedback prompts. Only if you choose to answer the short GravityOps survey or open the review prompt, your answers, or the plugin and version being reviewed, are sent to brightleafdigital.io.
  • Support access. Only if you grant BrightLeaf Digital support access, TrustedLogin creates a temporary login and notifies BrightLeaf Digital through TrustedLogin and brightleafdigital.io.
  • Freemius. Licensing and updates for the premium version run through Freemius. In the free version, Freemius receives information only if you opt in when activating the plugin: your name and email address, your site’s URL, your WordPress, PHP and plugin versions, and plugin events such as activation and deactivation. You can skip the opt-in and the plugin works the same.

BrightLeaf Digital: Privacy Policy. TrustedLogin: Authorized User Terms, Privacy Policy. Freemius: Terms, Privacy Policy.
sections.changelog:
1.5.0 | Nov 10, 2026

  • Unsubscribe links now open a confirmation page with an Unsubscribe button, so email security scanners and link previews can no longer unsubscribe people by accident. One-click unsubscribe from the email client still works without confirmation. Invalid or expired links now say so.
  • In the free version an unsubscribe now covers all mass emails from the site, as documented. Premium adds an Unsubscribe Scope setting: only the feed the email came from (the default, as before) or all mass emails.
  • New optional Mailing Address setting adds your postal address to every mass email, as anti-spam laws require.
  • For developers: new actions fire when an address is suppressed or unsuppressed, so you can sync opt-outs with other systems.
  • Updated documentation and support links.
  • Added an External services section to this readme describing when the plugin connects to outside services.
  • Updated the GravityOps shared library: the GravityOps dashboard now gets its product list, categories, links and announcements from BrightLeaf Digital’s signed online catalog, so new tools appear without a plugin update. Free versions offer an optional GravityOps Weekly newsletter signup, seasonal offers can appear on the plugin’s settings screen, and updating from the dashboard keeps a network-activated plugin network-active. Code Snippet Manager now appears on the dashboard, and premium updates explain when a license is required.

1.4.2 | Oct 11, 2026

  • Added documentation for the feed table controls.
  • Updated Freemius SDK to the latest version.
  • Tested with WordPress 7.1.
  • Updated the GravityOps shared library to 2.0.11, bringing a consistent Feeds screen across the suite, more reliable feed activation toggles and feed links, the Docs tab placed before Help, dashboard links that open in a new tab, and updated third-party components.

1.4.1 | Aug 3, 2026

  • GravityOps now asks for one short suite-wide survey instead of one survey per plugin, using a compact invitation and a dedicated dashboard form.
  • Closing a survey or review prompt now saves “not interested” immediately without reloading the page.
  • Fixed release packaging so distributed builds include the correct plugin files and dependencies.

1.4.0 | Aug 2, 2026

  • Moved global settings and batch management into dedicated GravityOps tabs: sending limits and batch retention now live under Deliverability, and batch monitoring, cron control, and batch management under Batches & Sending. The Mass Notifications entry under Forms → Settings now takes you there.
  • Rebuilt the Opt-In & Unsubscribe settings as their own tab, with fields that load as you choose a form and control field, plus a grid for mapping each preference choice to feeds (premium plans).
  • Fixed a fatal error when creating or updating a feed outside the WordPress admin, such as through the REST API or WP-CLI.
  • Tightened permission and security checks on the batch, suppression, and cron controls.
  • Added a Docs tab so the full plugin documentation is available right inside your WordPress dashboard.
  • Refreshed the Help tab with documentation, community, and support links.
  • The Account, Pricing, and Affiliation tabs now only appear when they apply to your license.
  • Improved the GravityOps dashboard with per-plugin icons, correct changelog links, update checks that no longer hold up the page, and a fix for opening a plugin right after activating it.
  • Individual plugin pages are no longer listed in the WordPress admin sidebar; open them from the GravityOps dashboard instead.
  • Updated the core GravityOps library for more reliable support access, interface fixes that are no longer served from a stale cache, and other small fixes.

1.3.9 | Jun 15, 2026

  • Improved the upgrade experience when moving from the free version to premium.
  • Added better safeguards for activating premium while the free version is still installed.
  • Improved scheduled email batch handling and cleanup.
  • Refreshed documentation and trial messaging.
